subject: Order Form redlines: maintenance carveouts, credit caps and response SLAs
messages:
From: Martha Lee <martha.lee@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Systems Legal <contracts@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form - SLA redlines attached

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the draft order form. We've attached our redline (Acme_Redline_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with several items that are blockers for procurement/legal:

- Uptime target: Acme is pushing for 99.9% monthly availability (your draft lists 99.95%).
- Service credits: we propose a monthly cap of 10% of monthly fees and that credits be applied automatically; your draft has a sliding scale without an explicit cap.
- Maintenance windows: we need scheduled maintenance limited to 6 hours/month and that scheduled maintenance does not count toward downtime credits.
- Emergency maintenance: Acme requests a carveout for emergency maintenance if we are notified within 2 hours and the maintenance is limited to vendor-prescribed patches; we also want a rollback option with a 30-minute SLA for reversing changes that cause customer impact.
- Response times: P1 response and mitigation commitments should be 1 hour for acknowledgement and 4 hours to mitigation; your SLA currently specifies 1 hour/8 hours.

We're attaching comments inline and would like a consolidated counterproposal. If possible, can we get a redline back by Thursday? We're running a procurement committee on Friday and need to resolve the credit cap and maintenance carveouts.

Thanks,
Martha Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Systems

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 10:03 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in Lauren (legal) and Priyom (solutions / implementation) to validate technical feasibility and legal risk.

Thanks Naomi — quick legal read and suggested trade-offs below (attached as RNW_SLA_Counterparty_Notes.docx). High-level: we can move on some items but need to limit financial exposure and operational risk.

Key points:
- Uptime: propose a differentiated approach — 99.95% for production/mission-critical routes (listed in the order form) and 99.9% for non-critical workloads. This lets us meet Acme's cost sensitivity while protecting default SLOs.

- Credit caps: we can accept a cap, but recommend a quarterly cap of 25% of fees (or an annual aggregate cap of 30%) rather than 10%/month. A 10% monthly cap materially increases our exposure for sustained outages.

- Maintenance windows: agree to scheduled maintenance <=6 hours/month if Acme accepts a 72-hour advance notice and a mutually agreed maintenance calendar; scheduled maintenance will not trigger credits provided notice criteria are met.

- Emergency maintenance: accept limited emergency carveouts but not an unconditional rollback SLA of 30 minutes. Rollback commitments depend on change class; propose a best-effort rollback time and escalation path (P0 on-call + hot-fix). We can commit to an operational rollback playbook and a target of 1–2 hours for common rollback scenarios, but not a contractual 30-minute guarantee.

- Response times: we can tighten mitigation for P1 to 6 hours if Acme needs faster mitigation than our default 8 hours; acknowledgement at 1 hour is fine.

Operational asks for Priyom: confirm whether we can instrument a maintenance calendar and automated notification to Acme, and whether we can commit to exclusion of scheduled maintenance from uptime calculations given our prefix/KV cache behavior.

I'll attach the legal notes. Naomi — if you want, I can prepare tracked redlines to the order form (will need the latest editable).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RNW_SLA_Counterparty_Notes.docx]

Subject: Consolidated counterproposal + revised order form (next steps)

Martha — thanks for your patience while we reviewed the redlines. Attached is a consolidated counterproposal and a redlined order form (Redwood_OrderForm_v5_redlines.pdf). Summary of remaining trade-offs: 

- Availability: Redwood proposes 99.95% for production routes as defined in Appendix A, 99.9% for non-production. If Acme can identify which ingestion/serving routes are mission-critical we'll mark those as production.

- Credit cap: proposed quarterly cap of 25% of fees, annual aggregate cap of 30%. We cannot accept a 10% monthly cap due to concentrated exposure for platform-level incidents.

- Maintenance: we accept scheduled maintenance <=6 hours/month excluded from downtime calculations provided Acme accepts 72-hour notice and a shared maintenance calendar. We'll coordinate blackout windows during your peak ETL cycles as requested.

- Emergency maintenance & rollback: we will provide an operational rollback playbook and target rollback windows (1–2 hours for common scenarios). We cannot make a firm 30-minute rollback guarantee in the contract; we'll commit to expedited escalation and a dedicated on-call for the first 24 hours post-change for production routes.

- Response SLA: acknowledgement for P1 within 1 hour; target mitigation within 6 hours (contractual).

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline and comment on the availability routing (Appendix A) where you want the 99.95% commitment to apply.
2) If this is acceptable, I'll generate a DocuSign packet for the revised order form and ancillary amendment. Link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/REVISED-ORDERFORM-ACME-2027
3) If you want to discuss, I'm available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT.

I've attached the redline for ease of review.

Best regards,
